FAQ

Questions athletes ask before they start.

What exactly happens in a Hyrox race?

You run 1 km, then complete one functional station, and repeat that eight times, so the race is 8 km of running and 8 stations. The stations come in the same order every time: SkiErg, sled push, sled pull, burpee broad jumps, rowing, farmers carry, sandbag lunges and wall balls. Weights change by division, and the format is the same at every event.

What is a good Hyrox time for a beginner?

Published benchmarks put typical first-timer finishes at roughly 1:40 to 1:55 for men and 1:55 to 2:10 for women, and averages across all finishers sit at about 1:35 for men and 1:50 for women. Your time depends on your division, your running and how well you pace the stations, so for a first race a finish is a better target than a number.

How many weeks do I need to train for Hyrox?

Twelve weeks is a common length for a first race if you already exercise a few times a week. If you are starting from very little, allow more time to build a base first. The free plan and the paperback plans from HybridX are built around 12 weeks, and the plan finder picks between them from your experience.

What is compromised running and why does it matter for Hyrox?

Compromised running is running while your legs and breathing are already loaded from the station before, such as a sled push or wall balls. Every kilometre of a Hyrox race is run this way, so you will be slower than on a fresh run. Practising it in training, as the free 12-week running plan does, is how you keep the pace from falling apart halfway through.

How do I access the HybridX app and what does it include?

Go to app.hybridx.club to start. The app costs £5 a month and the first 14 days are free. It includes daily workouts, a program library, progress tracking and Edge Coach.

Do I have to sign up to use the plan finder?

No. There is no sign-up, and the plan finder gives you your result straight away. If nothing it suggests fits, you can send us a message instead.
